extracted.intended_audience: researchers, grant reviewers, university community, and policy-makers interested in peer review fairness
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and evaluating methods to detect and prevent commensuration bias in grant application peer review, with attention to how multi-dimensional reviewer scores are combined into overall scores and to producing policy recommendations for fair review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring applications along multiple dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant proposal review procedures commonly require reviewers to score applications along multiple dimensions -- for example, a proposal's approach, innovation, versus significance -- as an intermediate step in determining the proposal's overall score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These multi-criterion scores are used as inputs to produce an overall score; examples explicitly mentioned are 'approach', 'innovation', and 'significance'. The page frames this multi-dimensional scoring as a common procedural feature of grant peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation/combination of individual dimension scores
rubrics_metrics.description: When procedures are left unspecified for how reviewers should combine individual scores (along multiple dimensions) into overall scores, evaluators might arrive at overall scores in ways that subtly advantage and disadvantage grant proposals submitted by applicants from different social groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lack of specified aggregation rules is identified as a procedural vulnerability. Explicit, consistent aggregation/combination methods (or policies) are implied as necessary to avoid variable, potentially biased overall evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commensuration bias (detection and definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any such difference is what we call commensuration bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined on the page as differences in overall scores across social groups resulting from how multiple-dimension scores are combined. The funded project aims to develop methodology to detect this form of bias in grant peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness / equity in grant peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer concrete, efficient policies that ensure fair review for any grant agency that requires scoring of applications along multiple criteria, including the National Institutes of Health (NIH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stated goal is to translate detection methods into policy recommendations that improve fairness and effectiveness of review processes so they do not subtly advantage or disadvantage applicants from different social groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF review criterion: Intellectual Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit ... review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the two high-level NSF evaluation dimensions used to assess the award; implies proposals should address intellectual merit to be competitive for NSF funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF review criterion: Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: This award ... has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's ... broader impacts review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the second of NSF's two principal review criteria; proposals are expected to articulate broader impacts in addition to intellectual merit.
